solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Like a sort of view showing a main crop ruined

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked and put back together differently, so the letters get rearranged

parts.note: the nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A farmer surveys a wide landscape where the main harvest has been destroyed.
explanation.definitionFit: A panoramic view is a sweeping wide-angle one, so the adjective describes that sort of outlook.

clue.text: European police — not in charge

indicators.note: saying not before a phrase means that phrase is taken away from the word before it

parts.note: taken as written
IC is the standard abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A continental police force that has nobody running it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pole is a person from Poland, a country of Europe, so the noun names one kind of European.

clue.text: Fresh wine for many a town

parts.note: fresh means new
port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: New wine is supplied to plenty of towns.
explanation.definitionFit: Several places in Wales, England, the USA and elsewhere carry the name Newport, hence many a town.

clue.text: Grass you once found below river

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed below another comes after it in the grid

parts.note: R is the usual abbreviation for river
ye is the old plural form of you

explanation.surface: Someone long ago discovered grass growing beneath a riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye is a cereal plant, and cereals belong to the grass family botanically.

clue.text: Lose maiden on Scottish island

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
Islay is an island of the Inner Hebrides, famous for whisky

explanation.surface: A young woman goes missing on a Hebridean island.
explanation.definitionFit: To mislay something is to put it somewhere and forget where, so you lose track of it.

clue.text: Betrayed prisoner, angry being locked up

indicators.note: whatever is locked up sits inside something else, here inside the word for prisoner

parts.note: con is short for convict
a heated person is angry

explanation.surface: A furious inmate has been jailed after being double-crossed.
explanation.walkthrough: The two-letter tail of the answer comes from splitting the prisoner word around the angry one, so the space falls inside a block.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cheated on is to have a partner unfaithful to you, which is a form of being betrayed.

clue.text: Fish firm foremost with deliveries

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: foremost picks out what comes at the very front of the following word

parts.note: the leading letter of the word

explanation.surface: A fishmonger's business leads the way with its deliveries.
explanation.definitionFit: Cod is a common white-fleshed sea creature caught in the North Atlantic.

clue.text: Counters offering cooked food

definitions.meaning: first meaning: tokens used for betting at a casino
second meaning: fried strips of potato

explanation.surface: Shop counters where hot food is served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counters' looks like shop counters, but it means gaming tokens. In Britain chips are what Americans call fries.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both gambling tokens and fried potato strips, the British side dish.

clue.text: Hate getting low grades on exam

parts.note: D and E are poor marks on a grading scale
an exam is a test

explanation.surface: A student loathes getting poor marks in an examination.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest is to loathe intensely, a strong synonym for the verb.

clue.text: Without blemish? Not female acting illegally

indicators.note: not with a word naming something means that thing is left out

parts.note: something without a blemish has no flaw
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: Someone who seemed perfect, but who is not a woman, turns out to be a criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawless person disregards the rules of society, which is behaving like a criminal.

clue.text: Poet and priest presented with holy books

parts.note: Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible
OT is the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A poet and a clergyman are given copies of scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: T. S. Eliot wrote The Waste Land, making him a famous twentieth-century writer of verse.

clue.text: Top artist involved with Sir — artist being one of these?

definitions.note: singular in the clue, read as naming the class: an artist painting Sir is one of these

indicators.note: involved suggests things tangled together, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A leading painter is commissioned to paint a knight, so presumably works in that genre.
explanation.definitionFit: Portraitists are painters of likenesses, and painting a knight is the kind of commission they take.

clue.text: Stare with Latin tricky? One misses out — unable to do this?

indicators.note: something tricky is twisted and devious, so the letters are jumbled
one is a common way to say the numeral, and missing out means it is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A student stares at a hard Latin passage, failing to render it into English.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the I from LATIN, then rearrange STARE and LATN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone staring at difficult Latin is unable to render it into their own language, which is to translate.

clue.text: Visitors to Athens come across this

definitions.text: Visitors to Athens come across this

indicators.note: to come across is to find, and the answer is found spread over adjacent words

parts.note: the letters straddle the end of the first word and the next two

explanation.surface: Tourists in Athens inevitably come upon a certain feature.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: tourists to Athens do encounter the ancient colonnades.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoa is a covered colonnade of ancient Greece, and the Athens ruins of such porticoes attract tourists.

clue.text: Fellow initially brought in by police investigator as expert

indicators.note: something brought in by another goes inside it

parts.note: Det is the abbreviation for detective

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A man is called in by a detective to serve as a specialist witness.
explanation.definitionFit: Deft means skilful and nimble with the hands, so an expert performer is deft.

clue.text: A lot of money for piece of music

parts.note: taken as written
a tune is a melody

explanation.surface: Someone is paid a huge sum for a composition.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortune is a very large sum of wealth, as in 'it cost a fortune'.

clue.text: Eats quickly in barracks

definitions.meaning: first meaning: wolfs food down greedily

explanation.surface: Soldiers bolt down their meals in their living quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barracks' looks like a noun for army quarters, but here it is a verb: to barrack is to jeer at a speaker or player.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both gobbling food greedily and jeering derisively at someone.

clue.text: Pretentious person rose up unexpectedly

indicators.note: something occurring unexpectedly comes out in a surprising form, so letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A show-off suddenly stood up.
explanation.definitionFit: A poseur strikes attitudes to impress others, affecting a manner they do not really have.

clue.text: Nation that's initially angry over hill and dale?

indicators.note: initially says one piece comes at the start, before the other piece

parts.note: cross means annoyed
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: A country whose first response is fury spread over its landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' looks like it wants a first letter, but it only says the angry word goes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross-country route goes across open fields and hills rather than along roads.

clue.text: Smell nothing grim

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
dour means stern and gloomy

explanation.surface: A scent that is not unpleasant at all.
explanation.definitionFit: An odour is a scent or whiff of something, usually an unpleasant one.

clue.text: Cockney cads — slippery types

indicators.note: a Cockney, a working-class Londoner, traditionally drops the H at the start of words

parts.note: a heel is a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: East End rogues described as shifty characters.
explanation.walkthrough: Without its H, HEELS becomes EELS.
explanation.definitionFit: These snake-like fish are notoriously hard to grip, so they are literally slimy creatures.

clue.text: Woman supporting a learner being kept in

indicators.note: a thing kept in is held inside the other pieces

parts.note: if you support something you are for it
taken as written
L is for learner, as on a learner driver's L-plate

explanation.surface: A woman backs a student who has been held behind after school.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes inside FOR A, giving F-L-ORA.
explanation.definitionFit: Flora is a female first name, so a woman could be called it.

clue.text: Wearing away with time, certainly

parts.note: an era is a period of time
sure means certainly, as in 'sure, I'll come'

explanation.surface: Something definitely erodes as the years pass.
explanation.definitionFit: An erasure is a rubbing out or removal, which is the act of wearing something off.

clue.text: Boxer limited by substantial injuries

indicators.note: something limited by words is confined within them, sitting across their boundary

parts.note: the letters sit across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A fighter is held back by serious wounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Muhammad Ali was the heavyweight champion, perhaps the most famous fighter in the ring.

clue.text: Gentleman showing some desire

indicators.note: some means only part of the next word is taken

parts.note: the middle three letters of the word

explanation.surface: A man displays a little longing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir is the polite form of address for a man, so it stands for a gentleman.

clue.text: Lord, one by loch, being present before expected time?

parts.note: an earl is a nobleman, a lord
I is the Roman numeral for one
Loch Ness is the Scottish lake of monster fame

explanation.surface: A nobleman stands beside a Scottish lake, arriving ahead of schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: Earliness is the quality of arriving or happening ahead of the scheduled moment.
